company.name: YNMO
company.shortDescription: First Arabic/English digital solution that aims to improve the quality of care and educational services for individuals with special needs
company.description:
YNMO is the first Arabic/English digital solution that aims to improve the quality of care and educational services for individuals with special needs by allowing service providers such as schools, centers & clinics to design and monitor individualized treatment plans.
Ynmo's mobile App also helps families screen their children through various screening tools (MCHAT - CDI - ASQ3) targeting Autism, language delay, and general developmental delay.

productsAndServices.description: A mobile application for parents to track their child's development across motor, cognitive, linguistic, emotional, and social domains, with access to online consultations from child development specialists.
productsAndServices.name: Ynmo Tifli

productsAndServices.description: A comprehensive management system for childcare centers that handles enrollment, family communication, attendance tracking, and billing on a unified platform.
productsAndServices.name: Ynmo Daycare

productsAndServices.description: A digital service for professional rehabilitation and education of children with disabilities, enabling flexible creation and management of individualized programs based on current curricula and standards.
productsAndServices.name: Ynmo Plan

productsAndServices.description: A set of tools including local and international scales for professional assessment of children's skills, accompanied by customizable accredited curricula.

insights.statement: The latest disclosed Series A round raised $5,000,000, or 69.86% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $775,298 to $27,427,889, a 35.38x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.
